scenes.say: 12 minutes out of the Cancún airport, your rental car and a taxi bump.
At 4 miles an hour, the taxi driver still climbs out holding his neck.
3 minutes later, a police truck pulls up behind you with its lights on.
Your life at every level of a rental car crash in Mexico starts here.

note_card.text: STATE DEPT: UNINSURED DRIVERS IN CRASHES MAY BE ARRESTED

scenes.say: By the end, you'll know what the taxi's dash camera saw.
On its windshield, a red light blinks once every 2 seconds, and nobody mentions it.
Officer Ríos asks for your license, your rental papers and your Mexican insurance.
Your license is fine. The State Department says a U.S. driver's license is valid in Mexico, so that part takes 10 seconds.

note_card.text: U.S. DRIVER'S LICENSES ARE VALID IN MEXICO (STATE DEPT)

scenes.say: Then you hold up your phone with your car insurance card from home, and Ríos shakes his head slowly without even reading it.
The State Department's page on Mexico is blunt about this. Mexican car insurance is required for all vehicles.

visual.head: U.S. GOVERNMENT
visual.text: Mexican car insurance, for all vehicles
visual.source: U.S. State Dept, Mexico Travel Advisory (2026)

scenes.say: Level one. The roundabout.
The same page has the line that matters most right now. Uninsured drivers involved in car accidents, major or minor, may be subject to arrest.

visual.head: U.S. GOVERNMENT
visual.text: uninsured drivers in accidents, major or minor
visual.source: U.S. State Dept, Mexico Travel Advisory (2026)

scenes.say: The same page says something worse for you. Arrests can happen regardless of who is at fault.

visual.text: arrests can happen regardless of who is at fault
visual.source: U.S. State Dept, Mexico Travel Advisory (2026)

scenes.say: Héctor, the taxi driver, tells Ríos in fast Spanish that you hit him from behind. You catch the word atrás, behind, and not much else.
You were sure the taxi rolled backward into you while you waited, but your foot was on the brake and you didn't see his wheels.
Ríos says something to his partner and gestures at the truck. In broken English, he tells you to relax, because it's only paperwork.

note_card.text: STATE DEPT: ARRESTS CAN HAPPEN REGARDLESS OF WHO IS AT FAULT

scenes.say: Level two. The yellow copy.
Ríos asks for the rental contract. It's in the glove box, a yellow carbon copy folded in 4 with your initials in 6 places.
Next to a line called third party liability, your initials sit beside the word declined. 19 dollars a day you decided not to pay.

note_card.text: THIRD PARTY LIABILITY: DECLINED

scenes.say: At the counter that morning, the agent asked twice if you were sure. You said your card back home had you covered.
Mexican federal law requires every vehicle on federal roads and highways to carry insurance that covers damage to other people and their property.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: insurance required on federal roads and bridges
visual.source: Ley de Caminos, Puentes y Autotransporte Federal, Art. 63 Bis

scenes.say: That same article puts the duty to buy that insurance on the vehicle's owner. Here, that means the rental company, which is why it was on the form.

visual.text: must buy the third-party insurance
visual.source: Ley de Caminos, Art. 63 Bis

scenes.say: What the form actually did was move the risk from the rental company onto you, and in a crash, that risk has a face, and it's Héctor's.

note_card.text: LEY DE CAMINOS, ART. 63 BIS: THIRD-PARTY INSURANCE ON FEDERAL ROADS

scenes.say: Ríos takes the yellow copy, reads the word declined, and puts it in his shirt pocket. Then he opens the back door of the truck.
Level three. The truck.
Nobody reads you rights in English in the truck. You sit on a metal bench, and your rental car keys are still in your hand.
Mexico's Constitution lets anyone detain a person caught committing a crime, or right after, as long as they're handed over without delay.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: a person caught in the act must be handed over at once
visual.source: Constitución (CPEUM), Art. 16

scenes.say: The same paragraph says the next stop is the Ministerio Público, the public prosecutor, and that the detention has to be recorded right away.

visual.text: the detention must be logged immediately
visual.source: CPEUM, Art. 16

scenes.say: A crash with an injury claim counts here. If someone is hurt, the question isn't only money anymore, it's a possible crime called lesiones.

note_card.text: CPEUM ART. 16: HANDED OVER WITHOUT DELAY, DETENTION RECORDED

scenes.say: Through the small back window you watch the roundabout get smaller, and the taxi's red light blink on and off one last time.

note_card.text: CPEUM ART. 16: NEXT STOP, THE MINISTERIO PÚBLICO

scenes.say: The truck stops outside a low concrete building with the word Fiscalía on the wall. That's the prosecutor's office, not a jail.
Inside, an officer writes your name and the time, 2:14 in the afternoon, in a large book and on a computer screen.

note_card.text: CPEUM ART. 16: THE DETENTION IS LOGGED AT ONCE

scenes.say: They take your phone, your belt and the rental keys, and they put them in a clear bag with a number written on it in marker.
Level four. The clock.
They put you in a room with a bench and a wall clock that runs 4 minutes fast. It's the only thing in here you can read.
Mexico's Constitution sets a hard limit. The prosecutor may hold you for no more than 48 hours before releasing you or bringing you to a judge.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: the most the prosecutor may hold you
visual.source: CPEUM, Art. 16

scenes.say: If a judge takes over, the Constitution gives the judge 72 hours to decide whether to bind you over for trial, unless you ask for more time.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: for a judge's order to keep you in the case
visual.source: CPEUM, Art. 19

scenes.say: And if the jail doesn't receive that order in time, it has to warn the judge, and 3 hours later it has to let you go.

visual.text: then the jail must release you without the order
visual.source: CPEUM, Art. 19

scenes.say: An investigator comes in with a form in Spanish. You say you don't speak Spanish, and he sighs and leaves to find someone who does.

note_card.text: CPEUM ART. 16: 48 HOURS MAX WITH THE PROSECUTOR

scenes.say: He has to. Mexico's national criminal code says that when someone doesn't speak or understand Spanish, a translator or interpreter must be provided.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: must be provided if you don't speak Spanish
visual.source: Código Nacional de Procedimientos Penales (CNPP), Art. 45

scenes.say: Another article in the same code lists it as your right, and adds that the interpreter is free, which matters when you have 900 dollars.

visual.text: a translator or interpreter at no cost to you
visual.source: CNPP, Art. 113, fr. XII

scenes.say: Two more rights sit in the Constitution itself. You're presumed innocent until a judge rules otherwise, and you may make a statement or stay silent.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: presumed innocent; free to speak or stay silent
visual.source: CPEUM, Art. 20(B), fr. I and II

scenes.say: An hour later the interpreter, a woman named Lupita, sits down next to you. You decide you won't sign anything until you've talked to a lawyer.

note_card.text: CNPP ART. 45: AN INTERPRETER MUST BE PROVIDED

scenes.say: The clock on the wall says 4:02. By the real time it's 3:58, and you have used up almost 2 of your 48 hours.
Level five. The embassy.
Through Lupita, you ask the investigator to call the U.S. consulate. He nods like he's heard it a thousand times, and writes it down.
The State Department's advice is exactly that. If you are arrested or detained, ask the police or prison officials to inform the U.S. Embassy or nearest consulate immediately.

visual.head: U.S. GOVERNMENT
visual.text: police must be asked to tell the embassy or consulate
visual.source: U.S. State Dept, Mexico Travel Advisory (2026)

scenes.say: Mexican law backs you up. When a detainee is a foreigner, the prosecutor must tell them without delay about their right to consular help.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: a foreign detainee must be told without delay
visual.source: CNPP, Art. 151

scenes.say: The prosecutor also has to notify the embassy or consulate itself and keep proof that it did, unless you and your lawyer ask them not to.

visual.text: the notice to the consulate must be recorded
visual.source: CNPP, Art. 151

scenes.say: Behind both rules is a 1963 treaty. If you ask, the local authorities must inform your consulate without delay that you've been detained.

visual.head: TREATY RULE
visual.text: your consulate is told if you ask
visual.source: Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (1963), Art. 36(1)(b)

scenes.say: According to the United Nations treaty records, 183 countries are party to that convention, so this rule follows you almost anywhere you travel.

visual.text: countries party to the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations
visual.source: UN Treaty Collection, ch. III-6

scenes.say: Night comes. They give you a bottle of water and a sandwich in plastic wrap, and you lie on the bench watching the clock run 4 minutes fast.

note_card.text: VIENNA CONVENTION ART. 36: CONSULATE TOLD WITHOUT DELAY IF YOU ASK

scenes.say: You think about the taxi's camera again. If it shows what you think it shows, why hasn't anyone asked for it?
Level six. The consul.
At 9 the next morning, a woman from the U.S. consulate named Dana comes to the visiting room with a folder and a clipboard.
The treaty gives her that right. Consular officers may visit a detained national, talk with them, write to them and arrange for their legal representation.

visual.head: TREATY RULE
visual.text: consuls may visit, talk with you and arrange a lawyer
visual.source: Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, Art. 36(1)(c)

scenes.say: You ask her the only question you've had since yesterday. Can you get me out of here today?
Her answer is printed on a State Department page. Consular officers cannot get U.S. citizens out of detention.

visual.head: U.S. GOVERNMENT
visual.text: get U.S. citizens out of detention
visual.source: travel.state.gov, Arrest or Detention of a U.S. Citizen Abroad

scenes.say: The same list keeps going. They can't tell a court anyone is guilty or innocent, they can't give legal advice or represent you, and they can't pay your fees.

visual.title: THE CONSUL CANNOT
lines: tell a court you're guilty or innocent
give legal advice or represent you
pay legal, medical or other fees

scenes.say: A federal regulation goes further. It prohibits consular officers from acting as anyone's agent or attorney, even when they'd like to help.

visual.text: consular officers may not act as agents or attorneys
visual.source: 22 CFR 92.81 (per 7 FAM 417)

scenes.say: Dana can still do a few things. She hands you a list of local attorneys who speak English, and promises to visit on a regular schedule.

note_card.text: CONSULS CAN: ATTORNEY LIST, REGULAR VISITS (STATE DEPT)

scenes.say: She also asks if she can call your family. The State Department says they contact family, friends or employers, normally with written permission from the detainee.

visual.head: U.S. GOVERNMENT
visual.text: before they contact your family, normally
visual.source: travel.state.gov, Arrest or Detention of a U.S. Citizen Abroad

scenes.say: You sign her form and write your sister Maya's number from memory. It's the one number you never had to save in your phone.

note_card.text: 22 CFR 92.81: A CONSUL CAN'T BE YOUR ATTORNEY

scenes.say: Level seven. The lawyer.
The attorneys on the list want a retainer you can't pay from a cell. So you ask Lupita what happens to people who can't pay anyone.
Mexico's Constitution gives you the right to a lawyer of your choice from the moment of detention. If you can't name one, the judge appoints a public defender.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: if you can't name a lawyer, one is appointed
visual.source: CPEUM, Art. 20(B), fr. VIII

scenes.say: Before noon, a defender named Ortega arrives in a gray suit with your file under her arm. She reads it standing up, then sits down.

note_card.text: CPEUM ART. 20(B) VIII: A PUBLIC DEFENDER IF YOU CAN'T NAME ONE

scenes.say: Through Lupita, she explains the two possible charges. Lesiones for Héctor's neck, and daños, damage to property, for the taxi's bumper.
In Quintana Roo, the state where Cancún sits, both injury and property damage are on the short list of crimes the law can punish even when they're accidental.

visual.head: QUINTANA ROO RULE
visual.text: injuries and damage can be punished as negligent crimes
visual.source: Código Penal de Quintana Roo, Art. 55

scenes.say: For accidental crimes, the state code sets the penalty at one quarter of what the intentional version would carry.

visual.head: QUINTANA ROO RULE
visual.text: of the penalty, for negligent crimes
visual.source: Código Penal de Quintana Roo, Art. 54

scenes.say: Then Ortega taps the file twice. The minor injury charge can only go forward if the injured person files a complaint, a querella.

visual.head: QUINTANA ROO RULE
visual.text: minor injuries are prosecuted only on the victim's complaint
visual.source: Código Penal de Quintana Roo, Art. 104

scenes.say: Property damage works the same way. The state code lists it among crimes that can only be prosecuted if the owner files a complaint.

visual.text: property damage needs the owner's complaint
visual.source: Código Penal de Quintana Roo, Art. 163

scenes.say: That puts most of what happens to you next in Héctor's hands, more than in the prosecutor's.
You tell Ortega about the camera on his windshield and the red light. She writes one word in big letters on her notepad, cámara, and underlines it twice.

note_card.text: QUINTANA ROO ART. 104: MINOR INJURIES NEED THE VICTIM'S COMPLAINT

scenes.say: Level eight. The number.
At 3 in the afternoon, Héctor's cousin comes to the office with a number written on paper. 2,800 dollars for the bumper, the neck and the days without fares.
Ortega explains the deal on the table. Mexico's criminal code allows a repair agreement, an acuerdo reparatorio, between the victim and the person accused.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: a repair agreement between victim and accused
visual.source: CNPP, Art. 186

scenes.say: Once the prosecutor or a judge approves the agreement and you've done everything it says, the criminal case is over for good.

visual.text: once the agreement is approved and fully kept
visual.source: CNPP, Art. 186

scenes.say: These agreements are only allowed for some crimes, and accidental crimes are one of them. So are crimes that need a complaint or can be forgiven by the victim.

visual.head: MEXICO RULE
visual.text: accidental crimes qualify for repair agreements
visual.source: CNPP, Art. 187, fr. I–II

scenes.say: There's also a window. A repair agreement can be made from the moment the complaint is filed until right before the order that opens a trial.

visual.text: the window for a repair agreement
visual.source: CNPP, Art. 188

scenes.say: You don't have 2,800 dollars in your checking account. You have 900 dollars and a credit card the Fiscalía can't take.
Dana calls Maya in Ohio. Maya can't wire money to a prosecutor's office, but the State Department runs a way to send money to a U.S. citizen abroad.
The money goes through the State Department in Washington to the embassy or consulate, by Western Union, money order or cashier's check.

visual.head: U.S. GOVERNMENT
visual.text: money for a citizen abroad goes through the State Dept
visual.source: travel.state.gov, Sending Money to a U.S. Citizen Abroad

scenes.say: The State Department charges a 30 dollar processing fee, once per fiscal year. Western Union charges its own fee on top of that.

visual.head: U.S. GOVERNMENT
visual.text: processing fee, once per fiscal year (+ Western Union's fee)
visual.source: travel.state.gov, Sending Money to a U.S. Citizen Abroad

scenes.say: Maya sends 1,000 dollars that night. It's her car payment, and she tells you not to say anything about it until you're home.

note_card.text: STATE DEPT: $30 FEE ONCE PER FISCAL YEAR + WESTERN UNION FEE

scenes.say: You still need 900 more, and the clock on the wall says 10:12, which means the real time is 10:08 at night.
Level nine. The camera.
The next morning, Ortega asks the prosecutor to request the video from the taxi's dash camera. Héctor's cousin brings a phone instead of a memory card.
On the screen, the taxi stops at the roundabout. Then the picture drifts slowly backward, and the hood of your rental car fills the frame.
The taxi rolled back into you. Your foot was on the brake the whole time, exactly like you thought, and the camera was recording it all along.
It doesn't undo the arrest. Remember the line from the State Department page. Arrests can happen regardless of who is at fault, and yours did.

note_card.text: STATE DEPT: ARRESTS CAN HAPPEN REGARDLESS OF WHO IS AT FAULT

scenes.say: But it changes the number. Héctor's cousin makes a phone call in the hallway, comes back, and crosses out 2,800 dollars. He writes 900.
You sign the repair agreement with Lupita reading every line out loud. 900 dollars for the bumper, and Héctor withdraws his complaint about the neck.

note_card.text: CNPP ART. 187: NEGLIGENT CRIMES CAN END WITH A REPAIR AGREEMENT

scenes.say: The state code says the pardon of the offended person ends the criminal case for crimes that can only be prosecuted by complaint.

visual.head: QUINTANA ROO RULE
visual.text: the victim's pardon ends a complaint-only case
visual.source: Código Penal de Quintana Roo, Art. 73

scenes.say: The prosecutor stamps the agreement at 1:20 in the afternoon. Counting from the roundabout, you were held for about 23 hours.
They hand back your phone, your belt and the clear bag with the number on it. The rental keys aren't in it, because the car is in a police lot.

note_card.text: QUINTANA ROO ART. 73: THE VICTIM'S PARDON ENDS A COMPLAINT-ONLY CASE

scenes.say: Level ten. The long way home.
On the plane, you read about the version of this story where Héctor doesn't sign, and the case goes all the way to a sentence.
Americans sentenced in Mexico can sometimes serve the rest of it in the United States, under a prisoner transfer treaty that took effect on November 30, 1977.

visual.head: TREATY RULE
visual.text: U.S.–Mexico prisoner transfer treaty in force (Nov 30)
visual.source: 7 FAM 480, State Dept Foreign Affairs Manual

scenes.say: There are conditions. The sentencing country, the receiving country and the prisoner must all agree, and Mexico requires all fines to be paid before a transfer.
Your consent is checked in Mexico by a U.S. magistrate judge. Once it's verified, federal law says that consent can't be taken back.

visual.head: U.S. RULE
visual.text: your consent to transfer, once verified

scenes.say: And only the country that convicted you can change or cancel the conviction. A U.S. court can't reopen a Mexican case.

visual.text: can modify or set aside a Mexican conviction

scenes.say: There's one more rule in that story, for people the government lends money to get home. If you default on that loan, your next passport can be refused.

visual.head: U.S. RULE
visual.text: if you're in default on a repatriation loan

scenes.say: Your version cost 900 dollars, 1,000 borrowed from Maya, 23 hours on a bench and a 4 minute fast clock you will see in your sleep for weeks.

visual.title: ONE ROUNDABOUT
visual.result: a $19-a-day box on a yellow copy

scenes.say: You pay Maya back in 4 months. She frames the Western Union receipt and hangs it in her kitchen, which you pretend not to find funny.
A year later you fly into Cancún for a wedding. At the rental counter, the agent slides the same yellow form across the desk.

note_card.text: LEY DE CAMINOS ART. 63 BIS: THIRD-PARTY INSURANCE ON FEDERAL ROADS

scenes.say: This time you initial the box that says accept, and you read every line before you sign, the way Lupita read the agreement to you.

note_card.text: MEXICAN CAR INSURANCE IS REQUIRED FOR ALL VEHICLES (STATE DEPT)

scenes.say: At the next counter, a man in a ball cap waves off the same line with a laugh and tells the agent his card back home has him covered.
You think about saying something, and then the agent asks him twice if he's sure, exactly like she asked you.
So answer this one honestly in the comments. Have you ever said no to rental car insurance abroad, and would you say it again after this?

visual.text: say no to rental insurance abroad again?

seo.title: Your Life at Every Level of a Rental Car Crash in Mexico
seo.title_b: Arrested After a 4 MPH Crash in Mexico: Every Level, 48 Hours
seo.hook: Twelve minutes out of the Cancún airport, your rental car and a taxi bump at a roundabout. This is every level that follows, from the roundabout to the day you find out what the taxi's dash camera saw.
seo.summary:
A 4 mph bump with a taxi at a roundabout outside Cancún, and you declined the rental counter's third-party liability insurance. This video follows a made-up American tourist through every level of a rental car crash arrest in Mexico, in time order: why the U.S. State Department says Mexican car insurance is required and that uninsured drivers in accidents may be arrested regardless of who is at fault, Mexico's federal insurance rule (Ley de Caminos, Art. 63 Bis), arrest in the act and the prosecutor's 48-hour limit (Constitution Art. 16), the judge's 72 hours (Art. 19), the right to a free interpreter (CNPP Arts. 45 and 113), silence, presumption of innocence and the public defender (Art. 20), consular notification under CNPP Art. 151 and the Vienna Convention Art. 36, what a U.S. consul can and cannot do, sending money through the State Department ($30 fee), Quintana Roo's rules on negligent injuries and property damage (complaint, one-quarter penalty, the victim's pardon), the repair agreement (acuerdo reparatorio, CNPP Arts. 186–188), the U.S.–Mexico prisoner transfer treaty (in force Nov 30, 1977; 18 U.S.C. 4100 and 4108) and the passport rule for unpaid repatriation loans (22 CFR 51.60).

Everyone in this story is made up, and so are the rental company, the taxi, the dollar amounts (the $19 a day insurance, the $2,800 and $900 demands, the $1,000 from Maya), the times and the dash camera video. The laws, deadlines and government rules come from the sources listed below. Real cases depend on the facts, the state and the authorities involved.
seo.disclaimer: This video explains general Mexican, Quintana Roo, U.S. and treaty rules for education and entertainment. It is not legal advice. Laws differ by state and country and change over time. If you or someone you know is detained abroad, ask the authorities to notify the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate and contact a licensed local attorney.

forbattring.forra_videon: Your Life at Every Level of a $38 Self-Checkout Arrest (K2lPH0w1HYk, publicerad 26 nov 00:30) – enligt PUBLICERAT_2026-11-25: 1 exponering vid 2 h-kontrollen; förra DAC före den: b1w06aHERrc 3 exp på 14 h. DAC 28 d: 663 exp, 3,8 % CTR, 4:37 snitt.
forbattring.problem: Två DAC-videor i rad har knappt fått exponeringar; båda är inomhus (trapphus, butik) med lokala delstatsregler som bara gäller en delstat (Kalifornien, Illinois), vilket gör ämnet smalt för publiken i hela USA/Kanada.
forbattring.andring: Ämnet gäller alla amerikaner och kanadensare som reser (hyrbil i Mexiko, ett av de vanligaste resmålen) och följer dagens trendfras 'what happens if you get arrested in another country'. Ny miljö (utomhus, starkt dagsljus), nytt rättssystem (Mexiko + delstaten Quintana Roo + USA:s konsulära regler + fördrag), en tydlig nedräkning (48 h-klockan) som håller spänningen över nivå 4–9, och en gåta som löses av ett föremål i första bilden (taxins kamera).
forbattring.forvantat: CTR ≥ 4 % (resa + Mexiko + trendtitel), ≥ 55 % kvar vid 0:30, ≥ 35 % vid 2:00, snittvisning ≥ 5:00.
forbattring.referens: Miles Unnoticed 'How Getting Arrested on a Cruise Ship Destroys Your Life at Every Level' (uKBrXDWCWlw, 11 694 visningar vecka 23/11, närmast i ämne: gripen på resa) + Honest Life POV 'Your Life at Every Level of Living Off the Grid' (678 751 månad) + Baldy POV DqyGPrK3LGQ. Transkript kunde inte hämtas: ingen Chrome i molnkörningen (youtube-transcriber kräver den), vidIQ 3 krediter (sökning kostar 5). Kroken 0/5/10/20/30 s enligt FORMAT_BLUEPRINT DAC: 0 s plats + hot i du-form, ~5 s polisen, ~10 s löftet, ~17 s gåtan (kameran), ~25 s första verkliga regeln.
forbattring.vi_slår_den_med: En verklig klocka från lagen (48 h, Art. 16) som tittaren ser ticka på väggen; 16 öppnade källor med paragraf på skärmen (State Dept, CPEUM 16/19/20, CNPP 45/113/151/186–188, Quintana Roo 54/55/73/104/163, Wienkonventionen 36, 18 U.S.C. 4100/4108, 22 CFR 51.60); och konkret, användbar kunskap för nästa resa (mexikansk ansvarsförsäkring, be polisen ringa konsulatet, vad konsuln inte kan, $30-avgiften).

hooks_kandidater.A_vald: 12 minutes out of the Cancún airport, your rental car and a taxi bump. + At 4 miles an hour, the taxi driver still climbs out holding his neck. (stakes + specificity; bild = miniatyren; siffror inom 5 s)
hooks_kandidater.B: A 4 mile an hour bump can start a 48 hour clock in Mexico. (curiosity – men första bilden blir ett kort)
hooks_kandidater.C: In Mexico, an uninsured driver in a crash can be arrested no matter who caused it. (contrarian/stakes – abstrakt, ingen person i bild; kommer i stället vid ~0:45)
hooks_kandidater.val: A – miniatyrens scen från bildruta 0, insats med siffror inom 5 s, löftet vid ~10 s; B:s klocka i nivå 4, C:s regel i nivå 1.

standard_check.miniatyr: FORMAT_BLUEPRINT DAC: 'LEVEL 1' vit + gul undertitel '48 HOURS', halvrealistisk man; hjälten ≈60 % höjd i höger tredjedel, 3 ord, ljus dagsmiljö; hotet (polisen + bilarna + kameralampan) störst; B/C andra bilder.
standard_check.krok: du-form från första meningen; plats + händelse + siffror inom 5 s ('12 minutes', '4 miles an hour'); polisen ~5 s; löftet i klartext ~10 s; gåtan (kameran) ~17 s; första verkliga regel (State Dept) ~30 s; ingen presentation de första 12 s.
standard_check.nivåer: 10 nivåer + slut: The roundabout, The yellow copy, The truck, The clock, The embassy, The consul, The lawyer, The number, The camera, The long way home, What it cost – varje nivå: första ögonblick → svårast → verklig regel → insidersanning → känsloslag.
standard_check.motiv: taxins röda kameralampa (0:12, nivå 3, 5, 7, löses nivå 9), väggklockan som går 4 minuter fel (nivå 4, 5, 8, slutet), det gula kontraktet (nivå 2, slutet), 'Are you sure?' vid disken (nivå 2 och slutet), påsen #27 / nyckelbricka #28.
standard_check.slut: gåtan löst (taxin rullade bakåt 2:02:14), avtal $900, fri efter ~23 h, men gripandet skedde ändå ('regardless of who is at fault'); fångöverföring + pass-regeln som den värre versionen; callback vid hyrdisken, cykeln fortsätter med nästa turist, fråga till tittaren.
standard_check.källor: 16 källor i beskrivningen; källrad på varje real/label-kort.
standard_check.miljöer: roundabout, car_interior, rental_counter, police_truck_back, fiscalia_outside, fiscalia_hall, holding_room, visit_room, fiscalia_office, sister_kitchen, airplane
standard_check.tittartid: första 30 s: 6 helbildsscener i rondellen (alla med walk_to), ingen medium/närbild, byte var ~4–6 s; första faktaskylten (note_card) vid ~16 s, första real-kort ~45 s.

notes.osäkert: State Dept-raderna ('Mexican car insurance is required…', 'Uninsured drivers … may be subject to arrest', 'Arrests can happen regardless of who is at fault', 'U.S. driver's licenses are valid in Mexico', 'ask the police or prison officials to inform…') lästa på State Dept-spegeln adoption.state.gov (Mexico Travel Advisory 29 maj 2026) – travel.state.gov själv nekade underagenten. Konsulns kan/kan inte-lista från travel.state.gov/content/passports/en/emergencies/arrest.html. Privacy Act-formuleringen undveks (bara 'normally with written permission'). '144 timmar' används inte (står inte i författningen). 63 Bis gäller federala vägar – manuset säger 'federal roads and highways'. Att lesiones i berättelsen är 'minor' (Art. 99, läker inom 15 dagar) och att Art. 104 kräver querella gäller just den första delen av Art. 99. Art. 189-numret för extinción ej använt på skärmen (bara 186–188). Fångöverföringsåret: FAM 11/30/1977 (ikraftträdande) – DOJ säger programmet började nov 1976; manuset säger 'took effect on November 30, 1977'. Att utredaren går för att hämta tolk, att ingen läser rättigheter i bilen, att kusinen sänker kravet och att polisen tar kontraktet är berättelse.
